parts.text: A student tries to make crystals of hydrated copper( II ) sulfate, CuSO 4 •5H 2 O. Crystals of hydrated copper( II ) sulfate are blue. The student makes aqueous copper( II ) sulfate by reacting copper( II ) carbonate with dilute sulfuric acid. The equation for the reaction is shown. CuCO 3 (s) + H 2 SO 4 (aq) CuSO 4 (aq) + H 2 O(l) + CO 2 (g) The first three steps of the method the student uses are shown. step 1 Pour 40 cm 3 of dilute sulfuric acid into a beaker. step 2 Add copper( II ) carbonate to the dilute sulfuric acid in the beaker until the copper( II ) carbonate is in excess. step 3 Remove the excess copper( II ) carbonate from the reaction mixture.
